reasoningSteps: Use a classic histogram with upper-inclusive boundaries 0.1, 0.3, 1.0 and +Inf seconds. The six synthetic durations are 0.05,0.1,0.2,0.3,0.8,1.2 seconds.
Cumulative bucket counts are 2,4,5,6. A duration of 0.1 belongs to the 0.1 bucket and every larger bucket; 0.3 belongs to the 0.3 bucket and every larger bucket.

Exactly four of six durations are at most 0.3 seconds, so the observed threshold fraction is 2/3. A classic bucket must exist at that exact threshold to use its count directly; do not invent an unconfigured boundary.

reasoningSteps: Model the element-presence behavior of absent(v) for an already evaluated instant vector. With no elements, absent produces a one-element result with value 1.
If v contains a series with value 0, the vector is not empty, so absent returns an empty vector. The same holds for a present value 7; absent tests presence rather than truthiness.

Thus a zero error count or zero queue length is not the same evidence as no matching series. Converting absence to zero without an explicit policy can hide missing instrumentation or collection failures.
